speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp is the only platform built to make your finance team leaner, faster, and better, saving businesses 5% annually on average so you can stay focused on growth.
zh: Ramp 是唯一一个旨在让你的财务团队更精简、更快、更好的平台，平均每年为企业节省 5% 的开支，让你可以专注于增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp just opened for business in the United Kingdom, so if you're running a business in the UK, you can now use Ramp's AI-powered finance platform to manage cards, expenses, bills, approvals, and accounting all in one place.
zh: Ramp 刚刚在英国正式开展业务，所以如果你在英国经营企业，你现在可以使用 Ramp 的 AI 驱动财务平台，在一个地方管理卡、费用、账单、审批和会计。

speaker: Unknown
en: I run my business on Ramp and so should you.
zh: 我用 Ramp 经营我的企业，你也应该这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at ramp.com slash invest.
zh: 在 ramp.com slash invest 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenAI, Cursor, Anthropic, Perplexity, and Vercel all have something in common.
zh: OpenAI、Cursor、Anthropic、Perplexity 和 Vercel 都有一个共同点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all use WorkOS.
zh: 它们都使用 WorkOS。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's why.
zh: 原因如下。

speaker: Unknown
en: To achieve enterprise adoption at scale, you have to deliver on core capabilities like SSO, SCIM, RBAC, and audit logs.
zh: 要实现大规模的企业级采用，你必须交付核心能力，比如 SSO、SCIM、RBAC 和审计日志。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where WorkOS comes in.
zh: 这就是 WorkOS 的用武之地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of spending months building these mission-critical capabilities yourself,
zh: 与其花几个月的时间自己构建这些关键任务能力，

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just use WorkOS APIs to gain all of them on day zero.
zh: 你可以直接使用 WorkOS 的 API，在第一天就获得所有这些能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why so many of the top AI teams you hear about already run on WorkOS.
zh: 这就是为什么你听到的这么多顶级 AI 团队已经在 WorkOS 上运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: WorkOS is the fastest way to become enterprise ready and stay focused on what matters most, your product.
zh: WorkOS 是让你最快做好企业级准备并专注于最重要的事情——你的产品——的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit WorkOS.com to get started.
zh: 访问 WorkOS.com 开始使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rogo is the AI platform purpose-built for financial institutions, serving tens of thousands of bankers and investors at hundreds of leading firms worldwide.
zh: Rogo 是专为金融机构打造的 AI 平台，为全球数百家领先公司的数万名银行家和投资者提供服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rogo's AI agents autonomously execute large chunk of your firm's workflows.
zh: Rogo 的智能体自主执行贵公司工作流中的很大一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can screen deals, draft SIMs, run buyer outreach, and due diligence on data rooms, all with full security and compliance handled.
zh: 它们可以筛选交易、起草 SIM、运行买方接触，以及在数据室中做尽职调查，所有这些都处理了完整的安全性和合规性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every action feeds Rogo Intelligence, the firm's context layer, turning years of deal experience into a secure, governed institutional memory that makes each new transaction stronger than the last.
zh: 每一个动作都汇入 Rogo Intelligence——该公司的上下文层，将多年的交易经验转化为安全、受治理的机构记忆，让每一笔新交易都比上一笔更强。

speaker: Unknown
en: To learn more, visit rogo.com slash invest.
zh: 想了解更多，请访问 rogo.com slash invest。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, Christina, I've been so excited to do this with you.
zh: 那么，Christina，我一直很兴奋能和你一起做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's been five years since we last did it.
zh: 我记得我们上次做是五年前了。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lifetime ago.
zh: 一辈子之前了。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lifetime ago.
zh: 一辈子之前了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been very successful in the intervening five years, so I'm excited to catch up.
zh: 在这中间的五年里我们都很成功，所以我很高兴能叙叙旧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you give us like the one-minute history of Vanta?
zh: 你能给我们简单讲一下 Vanta 的一分钟历史吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know we've done this before, but just to level set for people, when you started it, why, what it did then, how it's evolved, what it does now, quick overview.
zh: 我知道我们以前做过这个，但为了让观众有个基本了解——你什么时候创立的、为什么、当时它是做什么的、如何演变的、现在做什么，快速概述一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: It started Vanta about eight years ago, which feels about 8,000.
zh: 我大约八年前创立了 Vanta，感觉像八千年前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是啊，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like in 17 centuries ago with the premise of can we help companies build and own trust and build trust is like start security programs and compliance programs or mature them and then go get credit for their customers through audits like a SOC 2 or ISO 2701, HIPAA, et cetera, security questionnaires, trust centers.
zh: 你就像在 17 个世纪之前，带着这样一个前提：我们能否帮助公司建立并拥有信任——建立信任就像是启动安全项目和合规项目或使其成熟，然后通过审计从客户那里获得认可，比如 SOC 2 或 ISO 2701、HIPAA 等等、安全问卷、信任中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But basically this idea of can we build a security company by helping companies
zh: 但基本上这个想法是，我们能否通过帮助公司

speaker: Unknown
en: Implement security because it's what their customer is asking for.
zh: 实施安全来建立一家安全公司，因为这是他们的客户所要求的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we were initially known for SOC 2, Billboard.
zh: 所以我们最初以 SOC 2、广告牌闻名。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do have a billboard on the 101 that we were mostly known for making billboards, I joke, but it started very compliance, very audit-centric.
zh: 我们在 101 公路上确实有一块广告牌，我开玩笑说我们主要以做广告牌闻名，但它一开始非常以合规、以审计为中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea was always, hey, that's just one way to get a company started on this.
zh: 这个想法始终是，嘿，这只是让公司在这个方向上起步的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Since then, we've gone into different areas of security.
zh: 从那以后，我们进入了安全的不同领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've gone into different ways of earning trust with your customers.
zh: 我们进入了用不同方式赢得客户信任的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we're about 16,000 customers, global, with about five products.
zh: 今天，我们大约有 16,000 个客户，遍布全球，大约有五个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you win?
zh: 你是怎么赢的？

speaker: Unknown
en: This was a new category when you started, and I had to go through it.
zh: 你开始的时候这是一个新类别，我经历过这个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: My old business gets socked to compliant and certified in order to win certain accounts or whatever.
zh: 我的老企业为了赢得某些客户之类的事情，不得不去做 SOC 合规和认证。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it became an important thing kind of in the software era.
zh: 所以它变成了软件时代一件挺重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were many companies, I could probably name a handful, that were trying to do what you're trying to do.
zh: 有很多公司，我大概能说出好几家，在尝试做你正在尝试做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've emerged as sort of the only major winner.
zh: 而你已经成为几乎是唯一的大赢家。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you attribute it to over the last, since we last talked, like how did you win?
zh: 你把它归因于什么，自从我们上次交谈以来，你是怎么赢的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Execution, software, the blessing and the curse.
zh: 执行力、软件，这是福也是祸。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is more true now, even than it was five years ago, like you're really only as good as the last thing you shipped.
zh: 而且这比五年前更是如此，就像你真的只有上一个发布的东西那么好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can be first and you can start it and it doesn't really matter.
zh: 你可以是第一个，你可以开创它，但这并不真正重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was more true now because it's like someone can vibe code your thing in a weekend.
zh: 现在更是如此，因为有人可以在一个周末用 vibe coding 把你的东西做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you've just got to constantly be shipping new products, new features that make the experience better for customers running on that differentiation.
zh: 所以你必须不断地发布新产品、新功能，让运行在上面的客户体验更好，靠这个来形成差异化。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some feature level.
zh: 在某种功能层面上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the other thing we really invested in when it got competitive that was very good was integrations, pulling in data from other tools.
zh: 我认为当竞争变得激烈时，我们真正投入的另一件非常有效的事情是集成，从其他工具中拉取数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now you can connect Vanta to one of 400 tools.
zh: 所以现在你可以把 Vanta 连接到 400 个工具中的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We pull a ton of data out of those tools, and that's what powers the automation, the agent, the AI, all of that.
zh: 我们从这些工具中拉取了大量数据，而这正是驱动自动化、智能体、AI 等一切的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it our trust graph.
zh: 我们称之为我们的信任图谱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really just like a security data lake.
zh: 它其实就是一个安全数据湖。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is bigger, broader than any other provider, including some of the security providers, because we touch areas they don't.
zh: 而它比任何其他提供商都要大、都要广，包括一些安全提供商，因为我们触及了他们不触及的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in retrospect, that data foundation has let us build new things faster.
zh: 我觉得回头看，这个数据基础让我们能更快地构建新东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Software and agent.
zh: 软件和智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was that piece.
zh: 就是这一块。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think on the go-to-market side, it was like just keep pushing.
zh: 然后在 go-to-market 方面，我觉得就是不断推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good billboards.
zh: 好的广告牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good billboards.
zh: 好的广告牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shockingly good.
zh: 好得出奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Compliance that doesn't stock too much, which got really popular on r slash accounting, which none of us knew was a bucket list item in our lives.
zh: 「Compliance that doesn't stock too much」（不过度囤积的合规），这个在 r slash accounting 上变得非常火，我们谁都没想到这是我们人生中的愿望清单项目之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: When r slash accounting likes your things, you're like, OK, something worked.
zh: 当 r slash accounting 喜欢你的东西时，你会想，好，有什么东西起作用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the lived experience is just you can feel like you are going as fast as you can, and you should, in fact, lean in further and push harder.
zh: 然后那种切身体验就是，你能感觉到自己已经在尽可能快地前进了，而实际上你应该更进一步地投入，更加用力地推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the scariest moment?
zh: 最可怕的时刻是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The last 12 months, SaaS apocalypse.
zh: 过去 12 个月，SaaS 末日论。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, okay, great job building a system of record.
zh: 你就好像，好吧，干得好，建成了一个记录系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're now screwed.
zh: 你现在完蛋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're now worthless.
zh: 你现在一文不值了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're worth like, good job playing the game.
zh: 你的价值就像，干得好，游戏打得不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's some steak knives.
zh: 给你几把牛排刀。

speaker: Unknown
en: Parts of that are true and parts of that are not true.
zh: 这其中有一部分是真的，有一部分不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the vein of you're only as good as the last thing you shift.
zh: 有点像「你的价值只取决于你最近交付的东西」。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, great.
zh: 你就会想，好吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the agent?
zh: 智能体是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have all this data and a system of record.
zh: 你有这么多数据和一个记录系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fine.
zh: 那又怎样。

speaker: Unknown
en: What the heck are you doing with it?
zh: 你到底拿它在干什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: To say more about what that's felt like, roughly Vanta is a business that is growing very fast by historical standards with very high margins, which four years ago is considered like the best business model ever.
zh: 再多说说这种感觉是什么样的：粗略地说，Vanta 是一家按历史标准增长非常快、毛利率非常高的公司，四年前这被视为有史以来最好的商业模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing changed about that.
zh: 这一点没有任何改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're probably growing faster and the margins are still really high.
zh: 我觉得你可能增长得更快，毛利率也依然非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet the market has decided that the multiple for a business like yours is a third of what it used to be or a quarter of what it used to be.
zh: 然而市场已经判定，像你这样的公司的估值倍数是过去的三分之一或四分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: What has it been like to live through that as one of those entrepreneurs?
zh: 作为其中一位创业者，经历这一切是什么感受？

speaker: Unknown
en: Cognitive dissidence, you've got to hold two things in your head, right?
zh: 认知失调（cognitive dissidence），你必须同时把两件事放在脑子里，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, I think at the fullness of time, a 80% growth business with 80% margins will actually be better than over the same time period, run it out long enough, a 160% growth business with 30% margins.
zh: 其中一件是，我觉得随着时间推移，一家 80% 增长、80% 毛利率的公司，把时间拉得足够长，实际上会比同期一家 160% 增长、30% 毛利率的公司表现得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of these will like return more cash in the fullness of time.
zh: 随着时间推移，这两者中的一个最终会返还更多现金。

speaker: Unknown
en: But today, the latter is valued at 3x, 4x, the multiple of the former.
zh: 但今天，后者的估值倍数是前者的 3 倍、4 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 10x the multiple of the former, right?
zh: 甚至到 10 倍，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a part where you're like, hey, guys, everyone's being irrational here.
zh: 所以会有那么一刻你想说，嘿，各位，这里所有人都不理性。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a good business and you have to keep doing things that make business sense and doing the things that customers want, which may or may not be token pricing models that put you more in the latter category than the former profile.
zh: 这是一门好生意，你必须继续做在商业上有意义的事情，做客户想要的事情，不管那是不是会让你更偏向后者的画像而不是前者画像的 token 定价模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's like a very clear like game on the field piece.
zh: 然后还有一块非常清晰的「赛场上的博弈」的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if you need to be financed, again, you're looking at investors today, many of whom are kind of AI maximalists, talk to firms that are like, yeah, we'll invest in the labs and we'll basically invest in tractors in Iowa, nothing in between.
zh: 嗯，如果你需要再次融资，你今天面对的投资者，其中很多是某种程度上的 AI 最大化主义者，去和那些公司聊，他们会说，是的，我们会投资那些实验室，我们基本上会投资爱荷华州的拖拉机，中间的什么都不投。

speaker: Unknown
en: Robo-tractors in Iowa at a lab and like everything else.
zh: 爱荷华州的机器人拖拉机在一个实验室里，然后就是其他所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, huh, interesting point of view.
zh: 你就会想，哈，有意思的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from a like talent perspective, you hire ambitious people who want to do things.
zh: 而从人才的角度来说，你雇的是想做一番事业的雄心勃勃的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it feels like they're not in the right boat, they're going to change boat.
zh: 如果他们感觉自己不在对的船上，他们会换船。

speaker: Unknown
en: The talent war part is very real too.
zh: 人才战争这部分也是非常真实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you've just got to live with the fullness of time.
zh: 所以你只能顺应时势接受它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this will all sort itself out and you have to live for the
zh: 我认为这一切都会自己理顺,你必须为这个而活——

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's this funny fear that now like Bending Spoons is the Grim Reaper in the hallway, you know, meme or whatever.
zh: 所以现在有一种有趣的恐惧,就像 Bending Spoons 是走廊里的死神,你知道,那个梗图之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one wants to be a Ben Spoon.
zh: 没有人想成为 Ben Spoon。

speaker: Unknown
en: Love Bending Spoons, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句,我很喜欢 Bending Spoons。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's an interesting question of the Siren song right now is sell tokens via agents for security and compliance, I'm sure, or something like this.
zh: 我认为这是一个有趣的问题,现在的塞壬之歌就是通过智能体卖 token 来做安全和合规,我确定是这样,或者诸如此类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lots of thoughts on this.
zh: 对此有很多想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just so interested by companies like yours that were sort of winners of this last era that now have to make a set of decisions.
zh: 我对像你们这样上一时代的赢家、现在必须做出一系列决策的公司非常感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look at the 10-year rate.
zh: 看看十年期利率。

speaker: Unknown
en: The cost of capital is going up because you can put lots of money at really high return in AI stuff for the time being.
zh: 资本成本正在上升,因为暂时你可以把大量资金投入到 AI 领域获得非常高的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone looking at your business is like, well, I want higher returns or the same returns and I get that through agents or something.
zh: 有人看着你的业务会说,嗯,我想要更高的回报或相同的回报,我通过智能体或其他东西得到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk me through what it's been like to make the decisions.
zh: 跟我说说做这些决策是什么样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you thinking today?
zh: 你今天在想什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think of yourself as an AI business?
zh: 你认为自己是 AI 业务吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's that like?
zh: 那是什么感觉?

speaker: Unknown
en: So we do.
zh: 我们确实这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we go benchmark,
zh: 当我们去做基准对比时,

speaker: Unknown
en: Where we are from an agent in our product perspective against quote unquote AI applications, we have yet to find someone who is further along.
zh: 从我们产品中智能体的角度看,对比所谓的 AI 应用,我们还没有找到比我们走得更远的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could be like, we're doing a bad job looking is the obvious critique there.
zh: 你可能会说,最明显的批评就是我们找得很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are like constantly going to the set of names you imagine when you think AI applications.
zh: 我们不断地去看那些你一想到 AI 应用就会想到的那批名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And generally finding they're not yet where we are, where an agent is doing most of the work.
zh: 而总体上发现他们还没有达到我们的水平,即由智能体完成大部分工作的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's chat-based, but there's, like, long-running agents.
zh: 它是基于聊天的,但是,是长时间运行的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our agent is auto-generating UI on the fly, because sometimes you want chat, right, and sometimes you want UI, but we just have an agent that is building UI, user can do something, comes back in the flow, keeps it going, very much optimized around the, like, keep the user going in the flow loops.
zh: 我们的智能体会即时自动生成 UI,因为有时候你想要聊天,对吧,有时候你想要 UI,但我们有一个智能体在构建 UI,用户可以做点操作,然后回到流程中,让它继续下去,非常围绕让用户保持在流程循环中做优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I make sure I understand, meaning you are like a watchdog that's always on watching the security device programs?
zh: 所以我确认一下我的理解,意思是你们像一个一直开着、监视安全设备程序的看门狗?

speaker: Unknown
en: So we are definitely that, but in some ways you're like, you could do that in the past with just like monitoring and alerting.
zh: 我们确实是这样,但在某种程度上你会想,过去仅靠监控和告警就能做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is more like the Vanta product experience is now oriented around an agent that is bringing you as a user things and often saying, hey, I went and did this for you.
zh: 这更像是 Vanta 的产品体验现在围绕一个智能体展开,它作为一个用户服务,经常说,嘿,我去帮你做了这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you good with it?
zh: 你没问题吧?

en: There's a part of the market that is raising money every six months that 5x the prior valuation and that's a real talent competitor.
zh: 市场上有这样一部分公司，每六个月融一次资，估值是上一轮的 5 倍，那是真实的人才竞争对手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what about things like tenders?
zh: 那像 tender(要约收购)这类东西呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you done this historically?
zh: 你们历史上做过吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: We have not done them historically, but the game on the field is you're doing a tender every time and you got to do them.
zh: 我们历史上没有做过，但当下的游戏规则是，你每次其实都在做 tender，你必须得做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does this feel unhealthy?
zh: 这听起来健康吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全不健康。

speaker: Unknown
en: My opinions about it don't matter.
zh: 我对它的看法不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have all the feelings I want in whatever direction about tenders.
zh: 关于 tender,我想有什么样的感受都可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are normalized and people expect them and they expect it as part of their comp.
zh: 它们已经被常态化了，人们预期会有，并且把它当作薪酬的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you are not giving it to them, you got to give them a bunch of other stuff to make it up.
zh: 如果你不给他们，你就得给他们一堆其他东西来补偿。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does all of this affect your exit ambitions to go public or to be sold or realize some endgame for Vanta?
zh: 这一切如何影响你让 Vanta 上市、被收购或实现某个终局的雄心?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not at all?
zh: 完全没有影响?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not really, which is, again, a very founder-privileged statement, but the endgame is how long can we keep this going for?
zh: 基本没有，这 again 是一句非常「创始人特权」的话，但终局是，我们能把这个事情持续做多久?

speaker: Unknown
en: And 99% of the big independent software companies in the United States are public.
zh: 而美国 99% 的大型独立软件公司都是上市的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, IPO in that sense.
zh: 是的，从这个意义上说是 IPO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have it as a bucket list item myself.
zh: 我自己没有把它当作愿望清单上的一项。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more of like means to an end.
zh: 它更像是达到目的的手段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lots of people join companies and want the bucket list item, so founder-privileged caveat here again.
zh: 很多人加入公司并想要那个愿望清单项目，所以这里 again 附上创始人特权的免责声明。

speaker: Unknown
en: But Goal is a big independent standalone company.
zh: 但目标是成为一家大型、独立、自主的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: On all this stuff, tools for building, ways of building, kind of all these kinds of things I'm asking about, what do you think is overhyped and underhyped?
zh: 关于这些方面，构建工具、构建方式、我问的这类各种事情，你认为什么被高估了，什么被低估了?

speaker: Unknown
en: Underhyped is knowing the company and the customers relative to knowing the skillset.
zh: 被低估的是了解公司和客户，相对于掌握技能本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is still really hard to hire, train, onboard, make effective people who join a company.
zh: 招聘、培训、入职、让加入公司的人变得高效,现在仍然非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Company Marines make this better and easier and like put information at fingertips.
zh: Company Marines 让这些变得更好更容易，比如把信息放到指尖上。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there is still totally something to be said about someone who's been in a company, knows how to navigate the company, knows the customers, all of that.
zh: 但对于一个曾在公司待过、懂得如何在公司内部周旋、了解客户的人，仍然完全有可说之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm at a fuse right now where we value that skill set more than like the vertical skill set of you're good at sales, you're good at customer success.
zh: 我现在到了一个节点，我们更看重那种技能，而不是「你擅长销售、你擅长客户成功」这样的垂直技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And would take a worse salesperson on sales skill who knows the Vanta pieces more.
zh: 并且宁愿在销售技能上接受一个较差的销售员，只要他更了解 Vanta 的那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's something in that, and I think especially as a lot of the labs and fast-working AI companies are building out go-to-market teams, I think they're actually very much evaluating your good salesperson.
zh: 这里面有些道理，而且我认为，尤其是在很多实验室和快速行动的 AI 公司正在搭建 go-to-market 团队的时候，我觉得他们实际上正是在评估你所说的「好销售员」。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's slightly off.
zh: 这稍微有点偏了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think as we think about building agents for all of this, the company context piece.
zh: 然后我认为,当我们考虑为这一切构建智能体时，公司背景这一块。

speaker: Unknown
en: The customer context piece is probably being relatively undervalued to like you are a good salesperson with a less valuable skill slightly today than it was four years ago.
zh: 客户背景这一块可能相对被低估了，以至于「你是一个好销售员」这个如今的价值比四年前略低一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about overhyped?
zh: 那被高估的呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Token-based pricing, low margin for the sake of having low margins, custom training models for the marketing value.
zh: 基于 token 的定价、为了低利润率而低利润率、为了营销价值而自定义训练模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will you be able to say we post-trained a model on our stuff?
zh: 也就是为了能说「我们用自己的数据后训练了一个模型」?

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Explain why.
zh: 解释一下为什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go talk to the inference providers and sometimes give them, depending on the provider, give them truth serum.
zh: 去找推理服务提供商聊聊，有时 depending on the provider，给他们打一针真话血清。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will say like, look, the reason to post-train a model is cost.
zh: 他们会说，你看，后训练一个模型的理由是成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some businesses have that need.
zh: 有些业务确实有这种需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there is not a quality reason to do it.
zh: 但并没有质量上的理由去这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's kind of a marketing reason to do it right now in this environment.
zh: 在当下这个环境里，倒是有某种营销上的理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a lot of post training for marketing reasons, for investors and for customers, mostly for investors, actually.
zh: 而且我认为有很多后训练是为了营销理由，为了投资人、为了客户，其实主要是为了投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If one of those people were pitching the other side of this, the value of post training, what is the pitch to you?
zh: 如果这些人中有一个在向你推销这件事的另一面——后训练的价值，他们会对你说什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: One of these companies comes to you and is like, we'll do X, Y, Z for you.
zh: 其中一家公司来找你，说，我们会为你做 X、Y、Z。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are they saying?
zh: 他们会说什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what do they say the benefits are?
zh: 他们说好处是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: You are putting a stake in the ground of being a real AI company.
zh: 你是在插下一根标桩，宣示自己是一家真正的 AI 公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Customers will notice.
zh: 客户会察觉到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's the primary one.
zh: 我认为这是主要的一个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think there's a secondary one in some use cases of like a form factor thing.
zh: 我确实认为在某些用例中还有次要的一个，就是某种形态上的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think especially with large enterprises, you want to deploy this piece of software wall to wall that requires integrations and 17 people to sign off.
zh: 而且我认为尤其是大型企业，你想把这套软件全公司部署，那就需要各种集成和 17 个人签字批准。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oof.
zh: 哎呀。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a whole thing.
zh: 那又是一整套麻烦事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why don't you just give them a like model specific to them for this use case?
zh: 为什么不直接给他们一个专门针对这个用例的定制模型呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's semi-reasonable.
zh: 我觉得这算是半合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if I was one of these people and I came into Vanta, what does post-training literally mean?
zh: 所以如果我是这些人之一，我来到 Vanta,后训练字面上是什么意思?

speaker: Unknown
en: What would it mean in your context?
zh: 在你们的语境里它会是什么意思?

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you doing?
zh: 你们在做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the steps that you would go through?
zh: 你们会经历哪些步骤?

speaker: Unknown
en: So we would need a bunch of data from that specific customer and then go write a bunch of evals and change model weights based on that customer specific data.
zh: 我们需要从那个特定客户那里拿到一大堆数据，然后写一大堆评测，并基于该客户的特定数据去修改模型权重。

speaker: Unknown
en: The process would be they're trying to achieve something, they've got some data, you tune a model to achieve the thing, increase the eval, and then sell them that on an ongoing basis.
zh: 流程会是：他们想达成某个目标，他们有一些数据，你调优一个模型去达成那个目标，提升评测分数，然后以此为基础持续卖给他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your point is that that's overrated because it doesn't actually improve their...
zh: 而你的观点是这件事被高估了，因为它实际上并不能改善他们的……

speaker: Unknown
en: It can.
zh: 它是可以的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I'm skeptical in a couple ways.
zh: 我认为我在几个方面持怀疑态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, does everyone really want to be handed a model or there's so much around that from user experience perspective, from a deployment perspective, form factor?
zh: 我会想，大家真的想要被交付一个模型吗？还是说从用户体验的角度、从部署的角度、从形态的角度，围绕这件事有太多别的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels a little like, you know in the social media or mobile apps when we hadn't figured out, pull the refresh yet?
zh: 这感觉有点像，你还记得社交媒体或移动应用在我们还没想出下拉刷新之前的样子吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's something here.
zh: 这里面有点意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think anyone actually wants to be handed a model.
zh: 我认为实际上没有人真的想要被交付一个模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: The same way it's hitting a refresh button, I don't know if that sounds silly, but that's what we did in 2011.
zh: 就像点一个刷新按钮一样，我不知道这听起来是不是很傻，但 2011 年我们就是这么做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some version of that here.
zh: 这里也有某种类似的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: We haven't figured out how this actually works.
zh: 我们还没想清楚这件事实际上应该怎么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And handing models, I think, is not the right, reasonable iteration, but not the right solution.
zh: 而交付模型，我认为不是正确的——是合理的迭代，但不是正确的解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else like in the popular discourse that you think is crazy?
zh: 在流行的讨论中还有没有其他你觉得很疯狂的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: FDEs?
zh: FDE?

speaker: Unknown
en: I kind of think FDEs are crazy.
zh: 我有点觉得 FDE 挺疯狂的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a great talent arbitrage, the same way like Chief of Staff is.
zh: 我认为它是一种很棒的套利人才的方式，就像 Chief of Staff 那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: What FDE often is, is professional services.
zh: FDE 在很多时候其实就是专业服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think if you call it a professional services role, that's a very different talent profile than FDE in the current discourse.
zh: 但我认为，如果你把它叫做专业服务岗位，那在当前的讨论里，那是和 FDE 非常不同的人才画像。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you're not going to get the Harvard CS grad who's high agency and wants to go do things and learn how to build a business to go sign up to be like pro-serve person number four or number 12 at a company.
zh: 而且我认为你不可能让那些哈佛 CS 毕业、有很高主观能动性、想去做事、想学习如何打造一门生意的人，去报名当公司里专业服务人员的第四号或者第十二号。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a real job there.
zh: 我认为那里确实有一份真实的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think this FDE...
zh: 但我认为这个 FDE……

speaker: Unknown
en: Wrapping around it is probably not going to stay.
zh: 包裹在它外面的这层东西大概不会持续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: The company that we all think does as well is Palantir, which I think they probably do.
zh: 我们所有人都觉得做得很好的那家公司是 Palantir,我认为他们可能确实做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have eight-figure contracts.
zh: 他们有八位数的合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are some companies that have eight-figure contracts.
zh: 确实有一些公司拥有八位数的合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're using FTEs in a place where there's like five and six-figure contracts.
zh: 我认为我们在五位数和六位数合同的场景里在用 FTE。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those economics probably are upside down.
zh: 而那样的经济账很可能是倒挂的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in an, again, era of 30% growth margin better.
zh: 我们又处在，再强调一次，一个毛利 30% 更好的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that sort of works.
zh: 所以那种模式还算行得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: That doesn't feel sustainable.
zh: 但那感觉不可持续。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're at like a dinner in San Francisco with other founders, what are you talking about?
zh: 当你在旧金山和其他创始人一起吃晚饭时，你们在聊什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you talking about models and which ones to use?
zh: 是在聊模型以及该用哪个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the actual topics of conversation between founders right now?
zh: 现在创始人之间实际聊的话题是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's definitely like talent war pieces.
zh: 肯定有人才战争这类话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a time, this is more nine months ago, but it was the joy to go around the table and complain about Cursor, their taking of everyone.
zh: 有段时间——那是大概九个月前了——围着桌子转一圈吐槽 Cursor 抢走了所有人的乐趣还在。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's definitely that piece.
zh: 肯定有那一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a bit, I mean, I'll take FTEs of, do you actually do this?
zh: 还有一点，我是说，我接着说 FTE 的话题，你们真的在做这个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it working?
zh: 它能正常工作吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are you on this?
zh: 你在这件事上进展到哪了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, personal agents.
zh: 现在是个人智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which ones do you have?
zh: 你有哪些？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are actually useful?
zh: 哪些是真正有用的？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you think about the open source stuff, Chinese models, this, that, and the other, what have you learned talking to people around the world that are grappling with these same questions?
zh: 当你想到开源的东西、中国的模型，诸如此类，你和世界各地正在应对同样问题的人交流，学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I was with our customers in France a couple of weeks ago, which was lovely.
zh: 几周前我在法国和我们的客户在一起，那很愉快。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things I was very surprised to learn is a lot of the French software companies in Paris are using Chinese models predominantly.
zh: 让我非常惊讶地了解到的一件事是，巴黎很多法国软件公司主要在用中国的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I initially thought it was nationalism, maybe anti-American, you know, just something there and stupidly suggested that.
zh: 我一开始以为那是民族主义，也许是反美情绪，你知道，就是某种类似的东西，我还愚蠢地把这个猜测说了出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And someone very quickly corrected me and said, absolutely not.
zh: 然后有人很快纠正了我，说完全不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: We basically all switched to Chinese models when Trump closed Fable off to non-Americans.
zh: 基本上是在 Trump 对非美国人关闭 Fable 之后，我们都切换到了中国的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we just kind of realized there's a huge business continuity risk.
zh: 然后我们才意识到这里面存在巨大的业务连续性风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't trust that if we build a business on one of these American models, it will always be available.
zh: 如果我们把这些美国模型之一作为业务基础，我们无法相信它将始终可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we stopped doing that.
zh: 所以我们不再那样做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you dream the most about where the business could go over the next several years, what's the version of Vanta that could look like that?
zh: 如果你畅想未来几年这个业务最可能走向的方向，看起来会是什么样子的 Vanta 版本？

speaker: Unknown
en: We think of Vanta as a security company.
zh: 我们把 Vanta 看作一家安全公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Started with compliance.
zh: 从合规起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best version of compliance is proving the security you have.
zh: 合规的最佳形态就是证明你所拥有的安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got to have a good security.
zh: 你必须有良好的安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think we can and are moving into a bunch of security domains and sort of a platform pitch of like, look, we've already got the data.
zh: 我们认为我们可以、并且正在进入一堆安全领域，有点像一个平台叙事，就是：看，我们已经拿到了数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've already got the intelligence via the agent.
zh: 已有译文

speaker: Unknown
en: We can start stacking products on top of that and more security focused products.
zh: 我们可以开始在上面叠加产品，更多以安全为核心的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we understand the security of all these companies, the pressure on them to go prove they're legitimate and industrial grade is just going to go up.
zh: 随着我们理解所有这些公司的安全状况，它们要证明自己是正规的、工业级的压力只会越来越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one of the founding theses of Vanta eight years ago, but it feels even more true now.
zh: 这是八年前 Vanta 的创立论题之一，但现在感觉更加真实了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether they're working with enterprises, governments.
zh: 无论它们是在和企业、政府合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Regulators, lawmakers, you just have to prove your software's industrial grade in lots of ways.
zh: 和监管机构、立法者，你都必须用很多方式证明你的软件是工业级的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that will happen more and more in more and more ways in the future.
zh: 未来这种情况会越来越多、以越来越多的方式发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Vanta is the thing that connects both sides of that marketplace.
zh: 而 Vanta 就是连接这个市场两侧的那个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's the direction of security?
zh: 那么安全的方向是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is, of course, an incredibly interesting topic.
zh: 这当然是一个非常有趣的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early internet, everything broke, everything got hacked.
zh: 早期互联网，一切都坏掉，一切都被黑。

speaker: Unknown
en: This will probably be that times 10 or times 100.
zh: 这大概是那个的十倍或一百倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does security mean you compete with CrowdStrike and places like that?
zh: 安全是否意味着你要和 CrowdStrike 以及那样的公司竞争？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does security mean and what's its trajectory in this crazy era?
zh: 安全意味着什么，在这个疯狂的时代它的轨迹是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: These models just are so much more persistent than people.
zh: 这些模型就是比人坚持得多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will just try nine quadrillion things the way a person would give up after, I don't know, 9,000.
zh: 一个人大概试了 9000 次就会放弃，而它们会试九千万亿次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then in the course of that, they find things and chain things together.
zh: 在这个过程中，它们会发现东西，并把东西串联起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the discourse is around zero days.
zh: 很多讨论都是围绕零日漏洞的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's definitely some of that these models are finding that we didn't find before or didn't publicly find before.
zh: 肯定有一些这样的情况：这些模型发现了我们以前没发现的、或者说以前没有公开发现的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's more so happening is these models are able to chain 17 benign-ish or benign-on-their-own things together and then really find something.
zh: 我觉得更主要的是，这些模型能把 17 个各自看起来无害的东西串联起来，然后真正找到突破口。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you watch the OpenAI talk at RSA about hugging face, it's basically that.
